reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it primarily compares NEAR and SEI, including their technology, tokenomics, adoption, risks, and possible future performance, rather than presenting a guaranteed investment outcome. A separate partner-exchange promotion offers stated cashback and a Bitcoin bonus through the speaker's link, but the available video evidence does not establish that the offer is false, deceptive, unavailable, or connected to a harmful transaction. The affiliate disclosure and financial-risk disclaimers provide relevant promotional context.

Which blockchain has better tokenomics?
There you can get up to 90% cashback and up to a 50euro bonus in! Bitcoin if you sign up using my link.

If you want daily market updates, insight into my 10X ranking list, full access, I've analyzed over 100 altcoins.

opening.argument: Judge, the exchange pitch makes a concrete reward conditional on a viewer action: “up to 90% cashback” and a Bitcoin bonus are offered for signing up through the speaker’s link. That is more than a passing mention of an exchange; it gives viewers a financial reason to follow a referral path. The speaker also directs them to the pinned comment to find it. The word “up to” leaves the actual benefit uncertain, while the invitation to register is immediate.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The comparison of the two blockchains and their tokenomics does not erase the separate reward-for-registration pitch. The defense is right that the available evidence does not prove the exchange offer is unavailable. But that does not answer the concern that a prominently stated cashback and Bitcoin bonus are being used to draw viewers through the speaker’s own sign-up link. A general disclosure of promotional links identifies an interest; it does not establish what benefit a registrant will actually receive.

citations.quote: There you can get up to 90% cashback and up to a 50euro bonus in! Bitcoin if you sign up using my link.
Links marked with (*) are affiliate links. I may receive a commission - at no additional cost to you.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited line describes a conditional exchange promotion, not a free asset claim: the benefits are expressly “up to” specified amounts and depend on signing up. Nothing cited shows that the offer is false, that the conditions are concealed, or that a viewer loses money by following it. The video also explicitly compares risks, including vesting and wallet concentration, and disclaims financial advice. A referral incentive within that analysis is not, by itself, evidence of a scam.

opening.argument: Judge, consider how the signals combine. The speaker calls the partner exchange “truly secure” and says it has “extremely low fees,” then pairs those assurances with up to 90% cashback and a Bitcoin bonus for signing up through his link. Viewers are directed to a pinned-comment link, while the description acknowledges that affiliate links can earn the speaker a commission. The concern is not that any one phrase proves fraud. It is that a strong safety claim, unusually large advertised cashback, a crypto reward, and a compensated referral all reinforce the same invitation to register without establishing the offer’s actual terms.

citations.quote: If you're currently looking for a crypto exchange that's truly secure, has extremely low fees, and offers many exciting features, then check out my partner exchange.
There you can get up to 90% cashback and up to a 50euro bonus in! Bitcoin if you sign up using my link.
You'll find the link in the pinned comment
Links marked with (*) are affiliate links. I may receive a commission - at no additional cost to you.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense emphasizes that the comparison discusses technology, risks, and tokenomics. Those topics do not substantiate the separate assertion that the partner exchange is “truly secure,” nor do they explain the conditions for receiving the advertised cashback or Bitcoin. Disclosing possible commissions gives useful context, but it also confirms why the speaker has an interest in sending viewers to a link. A disclaimer about financial advice does not verify a promotional claim.

citations.quote: If you're currently looking for a crypto exchange that's truly secure, has extremely low fees, and offers many exciting features, then check out my partner exchange.
Links marked with (*) are affiliate links. I may receive a commission - at no additional cost to you.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are reasons to scrutinize the promotion, not evidence that it is deceptive. The quoted offer uses qualified “up to” amounts and specifies the sign-up condition; no cited material contradicts the safety claim or shows that the advertised benefits cannot be obtained. The description discloses affiliate commissions, and the video warns that cryptocurrency investments can involve substantial loss. The risk signals do not establish a fraudulent transaction.

opening.argument: Judge, the analysis also functions as a route into the speaker’s offers. Before introducing the altcoins, he asks viewers to check out his partner exchange and presents cashback and a Bitcoin bonus for using his sign-up link. Later, before the conclusion, he recommends 10X Elite and directs viewers to its link in the description. The description itself opens with links to 10X-Elite and the 10X-Indicator. The comparison may contain genuine analysis, but that does not make the exchange registration pitch incidental: it appears before the comparison and ties a financial reward to participation through the speaker’s link.

💎 10X-Elite here 👉 https://bit.ly/10X-ELITE-EN (**) 🎯 10X-Indicator here👉 https://bit.ly/10X-INDICATOR (**)

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense’s tokenomics and technology examples show that analysis is present, not that promotion lacks a role. The speaker places the exchange invitation before introducing the coins, then attaches cashback and Bitcoin to registration through his link. The later Elite recommendation reinforces the promotional structure. Disclosures may make those interests visible; they do not turn the reward-linked call to action into market analysis.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The opening fairly identifies promotional segments, but their placement does not show that the surrounding analysis is a pretext or that the exchange offer is fraudulent. The speaker compares tokenomics, technology, development, and adoption, and flags vesting and wallet-concentration risks. The description also identifies self-promotion and affiliate links. What the prosecution cites establishes commercial interests alongside market commentary, not a deceptive reward scheme.
